intro: You are standing on Hacılar, a mound in Burdur province dating back to 7000 BC. Excavated by James Mellaart in the 1950s, it produced the earliest and richest Neolithic painted pottery in Anatolia.
history: James Mellaart excavated the mound between 1957 and 1960, and the results changed the understanding of the Anatolian Neolithic. Its painted pottery ranks among the earliest and most accomplished in the Near East. But the story has a twist: the fake Hacılar vessels that later appeared on the market became a famous case of forgery in archaeology.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Neolithic house levels, the painted pottery and the female figurines, and look for the Chalcolithic wall.
facts: Did you know? So many fake Hacılar pots were made that, in the 1970s, thermoluminescence tests showed most of the pieces in museums were forgeries. And the painted pottery from the mound is among the earliest and most accomplished in the Near East.
outro: This brings our journey through Hacılar to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
